therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: redifferentiation of thyroid cancer cells to restore radioiodine uptake
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: patients with RAI-refractory metastatic thyroid cancer, with and without BRAF mutation
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: number of patients whose tumors acquire increased iodine uptake on iodine-124 PET scan; tumor response (CR or PR) by RECIST v1.1

results.effect_size: 12/20 evaluable patients showed new and/or increased iodine uptake; 5 partial responses and 3 stable disease among those treated with 131I
results.target_engagement_evidence: MEK inhibition by AZD6244 led to reacquisition of radioiodine uptake in 12 of 20 evaluable patients on iodine-124 PET
biomarker_changes: Mean reduction in serum thyroglobulin at 2 months after 131I: 89% (95% CI: 74.4–99.9)
Mean reduction in serum thyroglobulin at 6 months after 131I: 80% (95% CI: 5.1–100)
subgroup_findings: 12 patients showed new and/or increased iodine uptake on iodine-124 PET
8 patients remained the same or showed less iodine uptake
5 patients achieved partial response by RECIST v1.1
safety_signals: Serious adverse events included 1 case of gastric ulcer and 1 case of myelodysplastic syndrome

context.duration: 4 weeks of AZD6244 treatment; follow-up up to 6 months after radioiodine administration
